title: Look Inside Nested Cross-Validation
description: Course activity for Exercise 4: inspect, outer fold by outer fold, how inner cross-validation selects k and how the outer-test fold then evaluates that choice.
instructions: Choose an outer fold. The bar chart shows the inner cross-validation's mean MSE for every candidate k inside that fold's training data; the highlighted bar is the k it selected. The table below summarises every outer fold.
reflectionPrompts: Why can different outer folds select different values of k?
Which result estimates future performance: the best inner score or the outer score?
Why must the outer-test score not influence the selected k?
What would go wrong if scaling were fitted before creating the folds?
